blocks.text: After breakfast, transfer to the airport for the flight from La Paz to Uyuni, which takes about an hour. We will meet you on arrival to begin your trip across the salt flat.

Your first stop is the Train Cemetery on the outskirts of Uyuni. Its old steam locomotives and carriages date back to the growth of the region’s mining industry.

In Colchani, you will learn how salt is extracted and processed and how both activities shape local livelihoods. From there, you will head onto the Salar de Uyuni, the world’s largest salt flat. Its white surface stretches to the horizon. Look for the ‘eyes of water’, where water seeps through the salt crust.

Along the way, you will have views of Tunupa Volcano. You will visit the Chantani Museum, which explores the region’s natural and cultural heritage, and Incahuasi Island, also known as Fish Island on this itinerary. Giant cacti several metres tall grow on its rocky slopes.

Lunch is served at a table out on the salt flat, surrounded by the white plain. Afterwards, you will continue across the salt flat, stopping to explore the landscape and take photos.
Check in at Casa de Sal, a 3-star hotel that uses salt in its construction and finishes. Salt features are also visible inside.
In the evening, you will head back out onto the salt flat for tea at sunset. The white plain shifts from gold to shades of pink and lilac. Return to the hotel and rest.
